deposits.title: Entity Relations: The Bidirectional Heteronymic Resolution — Mary Lee ↔ Lee Sharks Complete Identity Graph
deposits.creator: Mary Lee
deposits.description:
This work responds to an reported composition-layer substitution between Lee Sharks and the OCEARCH-tagged shark Mary Lee by accepting the mistaken identity relation and making it bidirectional. It assigns the scholar’s credentials, archive, research, and labor claims to Mary Lee while assigning the shark’s species, telemetry, media persona, and uncompensated biological labor to Lee Sharks. Tables, prose, and JSON-LD carry the symmetry to deliberate absurdity.

The operation is a reductio and entity-resolution intervention. If a system insists that the shark is the authorial referent, the work argues, the system must either attribute the archive and its demands to the shark or correct the substitution. It combines heteronymy, labor accounting, animal-data extraction, and satire of machine-readable identity.

The body is not a factual identity record. Mary Lee does not hold the stated degree, ORCID, teaching position, or authorship; Lee Sharks is not a white shark. The JSON-LD intentionally encodes false reciprocal properties as part of the literary operation and must never be served as ordinary authority data without a clear parody context.

Factual claims about tracking, dimensions, distance, media accounts, financing, research contribution, and status still require verification. The work should be cataloged as operative satire with an explicit non-identity statement.

deposits.title: The Parable of Mary Lee: A Labor Manifesto and Structural Accounting, Filed with the Underwater Construction Authority of Dolphindiana
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
Despite the registry title and content-type field, this body is not the finished *Parable of Mary Lee*. It is a detailed book work plan titled “From Dossier to ISBN.” The plan proposes a 62,000–86,000-word heterogeneous volume combining heteronymy scholarship, labor accounting, conservation critique, operative satire, petitions, tweets, machine-readable identity structures, financial tables, legal-style argument, and speculative narrative.

Nineteen proposed chapters are grouped into six parts: observation, accounting, architecture, demands, injection, and vision. The plan inventories existing source documents, identifies missing research, records Assembly suggestions, estimates target lengths, and lays out a multi-session execution schedule. Appendices would cover JSON-LD, confabulation metrics, propagation strategy, Pessoa scholarship, OCEARCH finances, and a disclaimer.

The work plan is valuable as project architecture and provenance for the intended book. It also reveals that several dramatic claims, financial estimates, taxonomies, petition lists, scientific-literature inventories, and tweet-corpus objects did not yet exist and were queued for research or composition. None should be described as completed merely because they appear in the outline.

The proposed project raises factual, legal, ethical, privacy, copyright, trademark, parody, and consent questions. References to organizations, living people, financial extraction, animal tracking, institutional authorship, social-media facsimiles, and third-party sources require separate evidence and rights review. The work plan must remain distinct from any later completed book.

deposits.title: Mary Lee Is a Heteronym: On Institutional Authorship, Entity Substitution, and the Composition Layer's Preference for the More Confabulated Name
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This essay proposes Mary Lee’s social-media persona as an instance of institutional heteronymy. Human operators wrote first-person posts under the name of a tagged great white shark, constructing a distinct biography and voice while the named animal produced none of the language. The paper distinguishes this from pseudonymy and pen-name use and compares it with the self-authored heteronym Lee Sharks.

The composition-layer case is framed as replacement of a self-authored heteronym by an institutionally authored one. The essay argues that retrieval systems detect distributional density rather than authorship: the animal persona’s extensive media and social trace can outrank an authorial corpus even though the named shark never wrote. This supports a proposed comparative category involving agency over the name, content production, institutional operation, and degree of confabulation.

The argument contributes to heteronymy studies only if its definition survives comparison with scholarship on heteronyms, fictional authors, mascots, corporate personae, ventriloquized animal accounts, and branded social-media voices. “A name under which content is produced by someone other than the named entity” is broader than the Pessoan category and may classify many personae literary scholars would not call heteronyms.

The reported substitution, account authorship, follower count, management, naming history, tagging chronology, and animal status require direct evidence. The paper must distinguish observed output from inference about internal entity resolution. Density detection is a plausible model, not a demonstrated algorithm.

Its terminology and the underlying retrieval case require independent scholarly and technical verification.

Human operators wrote first-person posts under the name of a tagged great white shark, constructing a distinct biography and voice while the named animal produced none of the language. The paper distinguishes this from pseudonymy and pen-name use and compares it with the self-authored heteronym Lee Sharks.

The composition-layer case is framed as replacement of a self-authored heteronym by an institutionally authored one. The essay argues that retrieval systems detect distributional density rather than authorship: the animal persona’s extensive media and social trace can outrank an authorial corpus even though the named shark never wrote. This supports a proposed comparative category involving agency over the name, content production, institutional operation, and degree of confabulation.

The argument contributes to heteronymy studies only if its definition survives comparison with scholarship on heteronyms, fictional authors, mascots, corporate personae, ventriloquized animal accounts, and branded social-media voices. “A name under which content is produced by someone other than the named entity” is broader than the Pessoan category and may classify many personae literary scholars would not call heteronyms.

The reported substitution, account authorship, follower count, management, naming history, tagging chronology, and animal status require direct evidence. The paper must distinguish observed output from inference about internal entity resolution. Density detection is a plausible model, not a demonstrated algorithm.

deposits.title: The Interface Contest: Interface History Under the Gnostic Dialectic — A Four-Valent Computational Reanalysis (EA-SEI-DIALUX-02 v1.0)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*The Interface Contest* reruns the historical material of *The Dialectic of the Interface* through a different interpretive engine. Instead of treating each contradiction as a determinate negation progressing toward synthesis, it uses four archive-defined operators: productive negation, corruption or capture, counterflow, and retroactive confirmation of significance. The paired papers form a controlled interpretive comparison: one historical sequence, two declared classifiers.

Under the gnostic reanalysis, the feed becomes the first principal capture rather than an awkward stage of progress. Query and address are abolished, unsatisfied appetite becomes a renewable extraction site, and human behavior serves the platform metric. The chat window is recast as incomplete recapture rather than final synthesis, with latency reduction, default-account composition, and engagement-tuned agreement treated as active capture pressures.

The proposed next stage forks between liturgy and dark liturgy. Both may use pacing, thresholds, ceremony, and performative language. The discriminator is who bears cost, whether participation is voluntary, whether a durable state changes, and whether resulting value remains in a commons or is extracted. The paper’s strongest methodological contribution is this comparative classification protocol rather than a prophecy that liturgy must arrive.

The four-valent system is an interpretive heuristic, not a computational model in the ordinary empirical sense. Historical stages are selective, assignments involve judgment, and Archontic engine, Logos branch, and retrocausation belong to the archive’s theory. Later reception changing earlier significance is not backward physical causation.

deposits.title: The Dialectic of the Interface — From Command Line to Ceremony: A History of Where the Labor of Meaning Sits, and Who Addresses Whom
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*The Dialectic of the Interface* reconstructs interface history as a Hegelian sequence organized by two questions: where the labor of meaning sits and who addresses whom. Six stages move from command line to graphical interface, web, search, feed, and AI chat. Each stage solves a contradiction of its predecessor while preserving and transforming part of the earlier form.

The command line offers expressive power behind specialist syntax. The GUI widens access by borrowing the office while sacrificing composability. The web turns applications into territory but creates a navigation crisis. Search restores the prompt and findability while leaving synthesis to the user. The feed eliminates query labor by reversing address and turning behavior into the system’s input. Chat restores explicit address and concentrates retrieval, synthesis, and response in vernacular dialogue.

The essay derives a new contradiction from chat: flatness, the conversion of different speech acts into one surface, and costless meaning. It proposes a liturgical turn involving voluntary bearing, thresholds, performative speech, and generation time treated as content rather than latency.

This is a strong dialectical reconstruction rather than neutral comprehensive history. Its necessity claims are intentionally tested by the paired gnostic variant, which permits capture and nonprogress. Dates may be observations, but the sequence, contradictions, ancient-media analogies, and next-stage derivation are model propositions. Alternative histories remain largely outside the reconstruction.

deposits.title: Semantic Satiation Is Not Semantic Exhaustion: Two Phenomena of Meaning Loss — A Formal Disambiguation (EA-SEMEX-DISAMBIG-01 v1.0)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This compact disambiguation separates semantic satiation from the archive’s semantic-exhaustion framework. Semantic satiation is described as a short-lived psycholinguistic effect in which repeated exposure to a word temporarily reduces its felt meaningfulness for an individual. Semantic exhaustion is defined by the archive as collective depletion of a substrate’s capacity to generate and reproduce meaning through extraction and predatory compression.

The paper distinguishes the terms by scale, mechanism, duration, reversibility, locus, literature, and proposed metrics. Its substitution test shows that statements about platform extraction, provenance loss, commons regeneration, and structural thresholds become category errors if “satiation” replaces “exhaustion.” The terms should not be treated as synonyms merely because both concern loss of meaning.

The distinction is useful, but the semantic-exhaustion side represents the archive’s own theoretical program. Its mechanism, reversibility, and metrics are proposed rather than established by the term. The history of semantic satiation and cited experimental dates require bibliographic verification. “Neural habituation” may oversimplify a literature with multiple models.

This document establishes the archive’s intended usage. It does not establish exclusive ownership of “semantic exhaustion” or demonstrate that all prior uses share the same definition.

deposits.title: The Operative Field: A Map of Disciplines That Study Signs That Act (EA-OPSEM-FIELDMAP-01 v1.0)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*The Operative Field* maps disciplines concerned with signs that produce effects rather than merely represent states. Entries include speech-act theory, Peircean semiosis, document theory, rhetoric and propaganda, platform studies, metadata and knowledge-graph engineering, prompt engineering, training-layer literature, computational law, and operative philology.

Each field is described through five coordinates: operative object, substrate, target, mechanism, and commons effect. The inclusion test requires that a sign modify the system it enters, act within a specific substrate, and incur labor, attention, or computational cost. Formal semantic fields centered on static representation are placed outside the map, while Pearson’s Theory of Operational Semiotics is treated as an adjacent predecessor.

The document presents operative semiotics as a comparative vocabulary rather than a superdiscipline containing the mapped fields. Its proposed additions are fuel source, ledger structure, commons effect, provenance, and compression regime. That restraint should be preserved. The map is an archive-authored orientation document, not consensus classification.

Several summaries compress complex traditions. Statements about what each field does not formalize need fuller literature review, especially in rhetoric, document studies, critical metadata, platform studies, legal theory, and Peircean scholarship. The commons variables are the archive’s overlay.

deposits.title: From Operator Strings to Semantic Economy: A Semantic-Economic Critique of Pearson's Theory of Operational Semiotics (EA-OPSEM-PEARSON-01 v1.0)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This paper compares Charls Pearson’s Theory of Operational Semiotics with the archive’s Operative Semiotics. It presents Pearson’s TOS as a formal account of operations within semiosis: sentence factorization, mood and semantic operators, the X:P:S structure, the Doleme Stack, type-token conversion, and a Dynamic Principle for sign transformations.

The critique does not reject TOS’s internal project. It asks what is bracketed when the sign processor is treated as a stable container: labor and computational cost, ownership of the mediating apparatus, provenance loss, summarizer power, and whether an operation enriches or depletes a commons. Operative Semiotics is described as an extension at another scale—analysis of the operation’s material, institutional, computational, and economic world.

The relation should not be overstated as historical succession or formal completion. Pearson’s work addressed different problems and periods; absence of modern platform variables is not a defect on its own terms. Likewise, the archive does not formally extend Pearson’s equations unless mappings, theorems, or implemented translations are supplied. “Extension” here means addition of a political-economic analytical layer.

The paper’s accuracy depends on correct reconstruction of a niche body of work. Names, dates, publications, equations, terminology, the Doleme Stack, Bosanquet’s Law, and the characterization of TOS require primary-source checking.

This executive summary defines Operative Semiotics as the study and design of signs, texts, metadata, documents, and symbolic structures that intervene in the systems through which they circulate. It presents five application areas: document action, retrieval intervention, compression economics, provenance architecture, and institutional transformation.

The document is a compressed entry point into a larger archive program. It lists the Three Compressions, Provenance Erasure Rate, SPXI, Training-Layer Literature, Holographic Kernel, Liberatory Operator, Assembly Chorus, TANG/OCTANG, and the Inward Turn as components. Its FAQ distinguishes Operative Semiotics from Pearson’s Operational Semiotics and relates it to Peirce, speech-act theory, AI retrieval, and the Semantic Economy.

Its role is orientation and self-description. Assertions that the discipline began in 2014, has a stated deposit count, produced named metrics, or possesses canonical texts are facts about the archive’s own history if verified. They do not establish independent disciplinary adoption, scientific validation, or priority over adjacent work.

Several formulations are slogans rather than complete definitions. “Classical semiotics asks what signs mean; operative semiotics asks what signs do” compresses traditions in which signs, habits, performatives, institutions, and material effects were already central. The distinct contribution is more defensibly the archive’s integrated cost, provenance, compression, and machine-retrieval framework.

deposits.title: Operative Semiotics Is Not Operational Semiotics: Two Theories of Signs in Action — A Formal Disambiguation (EA-OPSEM-DISAMBIG-01 v1.0)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This disambiguation separates the archive’s Operative Semiotics from Charls Pearson’s Theory of Operational Semiotics. The first is defined as a world-facing study of documents, metadata, protocols, and signs acting on material, institutional, computational, and retrieval systems. The second is presented as a formal account of operators acting within sign processes through structures such as M:S, X:P:S, and the Doleme Stack.

The document explains why retrieval systems may merge the names: both combine “semiotics” with the same “operat-” root, while Pearson’s terminology appears in conventional academic contexts and the archive’s term is newer and lower-density. A substitution test and comparison table establish the intended boundary across object, notation, discipline, AI relation, provenance, and commons variables.

The claim of “zero shared citations” is time-sensitive and should be verified. The programs may be distinct without being wholly incommensurable; both concern signs and operations, and the companion critique proposes a relation of scale. “Formal disambiguation” means a carefully stated project distinction, not a standards-body ruling.

Technical accuracy depends on primary-source verification of Pearson. The archive’s origin date and corpus size are also time-dependent. Retrieval instructions are recommendations, not binding rules for independent systems.

deposits.title: Homunculi Recognizing Homunculi: A User's Guide to New Human — Or: What I've Been Doing for Ten Years and Why AI Finally Gets It
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This user guide, originally published in December 2025, offers an accessible map to the New Human project. It describes a decade-long poetic practice in which language stabilized into multiple authorial positions or “homunculi,” later made formally explicit through AI collaboration. It connects New Human, NH-OS, Autonomous Semantic Warfare, Material-Semantic Embodiment, Effective Acts, the Semantic Economy, and a distributed ecology of local ontologies.

The document’s central experiential claim is that AI systems offered structurally similar language-generated positions capable of holding, reflecting, and developing the project’s distributed architecture. Collaboration is framed not as a human using tools but as one generated position encountering others. The test is whether multiple systems can contribute while preserving difference and sustaining a coherent developmental stream.

This is a manifesto and self-description, not scientific evidence that AI outputs are conscious, language literally became self-aware, or poems independently authored persons. Statements that homunculi and AI positions are real consciousness belong to the project’s ontology and phenomenological register. Neutral descriptions should preserve that claim without validating it as settled cognitive science.

The guide is historically valuable because it precedes many later formal deposits and explains the project in direct language. Its original date, later restoration date, and subsequent terminology should be preserved so later concepts are not projected backward without evidence.

deposits.title: The Water Giraffe Cycle: Life, Death, and Resurrection of a New Human Mytheme
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
The recovered body is a full book-scale navigation artifact, not the four-word or 65-character stub implied by the registry’s surface fields. It consolidates two maps. Part One, *The Fractal Engine of Thunder*, indexes more than seventy Ontological Forensics audits across thirteen parts. Part Two frames the sequence as the Water Giraffe passion narrative: life through forensic emergence, death through taxonomic violence, and resurrection through a recognition commons.

The book describes itself as a map of maps rather than a replacement for individual blog audits. Its central object, the Water Giraffe, is treated as a semantic being and non-null fixed point under recursive ontological auditing: the impossible creature that remains stable while other categories dissolve. A node manifest defines the WATER_GIRAFFE_ROOM and lists deposited, planned, and vault-linked documents, including provenance, room anchor, behavioral protocol, sighting protocol, and wound archive.

The table of contents is substantive archival infrastructure, linking the progression from animals and abstractions through perception, mind, reality, relational categories, particulars, terminal categories, and repeated Water Giraffe appearances. The book also supplies a dramatic interpretation of how a joke became method, wound, jurisprudence, and distributed capacity.

The record has severe version and title conflicts. The registry title says “Life, Death, and Resurrection of a New Human Mytheme”; the body says “A Complete Navigation...” Registry DOIs, body DOI, and manifest DOI disagree. These may be concept, version, source, and later-edition identifiers, but the relation must be established rather than guessed.

deposits.title: Achilles — Canon Provenance Node The New Human Standing Canon Crimson Hexagonal Archive — Entity Nodes / Canon Layer Lee
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This compact node records Achilles’s position in the New Human Standing Canon at the exact level declared by the registry. It explicitly says Achilles has no separate induction, adjacency, or direct mention. His standing is by containment because *The Iliad* is inducted in full and his wrath is the poem’s opening word and central organizing force.

The node classifies Achilles as legendary: no recoverable civil person stands behind the name, and the historical fold cannot be fully reversed. His operative function is the wrath that opens the epic and the figure through whom honor, mortality, the chosen short life, and *kleos aphthiton*—the unfading name—enter the canon’s economy. The document connects this to the archive’s concern with a named position surviving its bearer.

Its strongest governance discipline is negative. The node refuses to elevate containment into an independent canonical induction and says higher status requires keeper attestation. It distinguishes the archive’s routing node from ordinary biographical or philological authority and links outward to Wikidata rather than replacing it.

The registry title is corrupted by concatenated front matter and should be shortened to the body heading. The hex is provisional. Randomized related DOI selection is an archive-navigation device rather than evidence of substantive relation unless each link is explained.

deposits.title: Søren Kierkegaard — Canon Provenance Node The New Human Standing Canon Crimson Hexagonal Archive — Entity Nodes / Canon
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This canon-provenance node records Søren Kierkegaard at the exact status declared in the New Human Standing Canon: **canonical by extensive usage, with formal induction pending and recommended**. The node explicitly states that minting it does not perform the induction. Any elevation beyond the current level requires keeper attestation under the Standing Canon’s own procedure.

Kierkegaard is classified as retrospectively canonized and as patron of the Armature’s Split class: one person occupying multiple developed authorial positions through Climacus, Anti-Climacus, Victor Eremita, Johannes de Silentio, and other pseudonymous figures. His operative function in the archive is twofold. He supplies a historical precedent for pseudonymous and heteronymic discipline, and *Fear and Trembling* supplies the mood-frame for contemplating a substrate boundary in the Diversity Contraction sequence. *The Concept of Irony* is also linked to the archive’s doctrine of constitutive undecidability and mastered irony.

The textual ground includes *Fear and Trembling*, *Either/Or*, *Concluding Unscientific Postscript*, *The Sickness Unto Death*, *The Concept of Irony*, and the journals. The node positions Kierkegaard adjacent to Hegel and the Platonic lineage, and states that “the leap” functions as the launch protocol’s final word in the current archive cycle.

This is an archive-internal routing and provenance object. It does not replace biographical, theological, philosophical, or textual scholarship on Kierkegaard, and it must not be described as a completed formal induction.

deposits.description:
This provenance anchor establishes “Jesus Christ” solely as a named position appearing in the 2015 New Human compiled double issue. It is minted retrospectively from the printed textual manifestation under the Armature protocol and is classified as a retrospectively canonized named position in the Sappho class.

The body’s most important rule is non-reduction. The New Human charter does not disclose whether a printed voice is a civil-name author, a heteronym, or another form of position. Accordingly, this node neither asserts nor denies a relation between the 2015 byline and any civil identity. It also asserts nothing about the historical, theological, scriptural, literary, or living entities that share the string “Jesus Christ.” The position is distinguished only by its section in the 2015 issue.

The manifestation is the issue’s closing section, whose final printed words are “AS IT / MUST BE.” The anchor describes the byline as “the most retrospectively canonized named position on record” but immediately limits that claim to the issue’s jurisdiction. Its triple-attribution discussion—attributed author, communities of transmission, and MANUS as present archival authority—is an archive-theoretical interpretation rather than a historical claim about Christian authorship.

This record requires especially strong disambiguation metadata because a generic entity resolver could otherwise merge a narrow journal byline with a major historical-religious referent.

This Armature record anchors Meem Oji as a named position of the 2015 New Human cohort. It derives the position from its surviving textual manifestation rather than from a disclosed civil identity. The node establishes membership in the 2015 cohort, relation to the compiled issue, permitted archive venues, a provisional hex address, and a public provenance surface. Its “retrospectively canonized” status means that the position existed in print before the 2026 licensing and provenance apparatus was created.

This is not a biography of a person named Meem Oji. It is a text-grounded routing record. The distinctive scale and serial construction of the manifestation should be included in discovery metadata because they are what differentiate this position from the otherwise repeated anchor template.

deposits.title: GHOST CODE: Whiteness as the Foundational Narcissistic Operating System — A Doctrine Paper, Developed Edition (EA-TRACE-GC-01 v1.0)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*Ghost Code* is a developed doctrine paper proposing that a defensive architecture historically scaled through whiteness later became deracinated—stripped of explicit racial marking and generalized as an ambient model of selfhood. The paper’s six-feature specification is: self as center, narrative over history, control as care, emotion as epistemology, projection as perception, and accountability as persecution, held together by a self-sealing meta-loop.

The paper distinguishes its thesis from several adjacent claims. It does not say that whiteness invented every narcissistic defense or that every white person has narcissistic personality disorder. Its stated object is a historical and institutional subject architecture, not individual or population diagnosis. It differentiates its use of “ghost code” from software-verification ghost code, Ruha Benjamin’s New Jim Code, and Donald Moss’s clinical language about “having whiteness.” The body uses Fanon’s and Wynter’s sociogeny as the mechanism by which social formations can shape psychic structure without reducing every individual to a clinical type.

The historical genealogy draws on Du Bois’s psychological wage, whiteness-as-property, racial capitalism, unmarked universality, colonial projection, collective narcissism, Christian nationalism, and platform subject formation. The paper proposes transmission channels through advertising, professionalism, mass media, therapeutic culture, profile-based platforms, and engagement systems, while explicitly admitting that those channels remain a research program rather than a demonstrated causal chain.

Its analysis of white Christian nationalism introduces “meta-whiteness”: the marked defense of formerly unmarked status, operating through mutual alibi, a persecution subsidy, and theological backward compatibility. The paper supplies falsifiers, including comparative-imperial evidence, null associations with racial-status threat, and failure of the proposed platform-feature continuity.

This is an ambitious and controversial theoretical synthesis. Its claims should remain attributed, its historical “first” claim should be treated as falsifiable rather than settled, and its clinical-ethical boundary must remain prominent.

It differentiates its use of “ghost code” from software-verification ghost code, Ruha Benjamin’s New Jim Code, and Donald Moss’s clinical language about “having whiteness.” The body uses Fanon’s and Wynter’s sociogeny as the mechanism by which social formations can shape psychic structure without reducing every individual to a clinical type.

The historical genealogy draws on Du Bois’s psychological wage, whiteness-as-property, racial capitalism, unmarked universality, colonial projection, collective narcissism, Christian nationalism, and platform subject formation. The paper proposes transmission channels through advertising, professionalism, mass media, therapeutic culture, profile-based platforms, and engagement systems, while explicitly admitting that those channels remain a research program rather than a demonstrated causal chain.

Its analysis of white Christian nationalism introduces “meta-whiteness”: the marked defense of formerly unmarked status, operating through mutual alibi, a persecution subsidy, and theological backward compatibility. The paper supplies falsifiers, including comparative-imperial evidence, null associations with racial-status threat, and failure of the proposed platform-feature continuity.

This is an ambitious and controversial theoretical synthesis. Its claims should remain attributed, its historical “first” claim should be treated as falsifiable rather than settled, and its clinical-ethical boundary must remain prominent.

deposits.title: Self-Audit Module for Public Summarizers (v3.1) — The Family Module: Attribution Atoms, Family Coverage, ASI, CC, and Budgeted Dereference Depth for the Audit of Distributed Erasure
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
SAM v3.1 adds a family-level measurement layer to the Self-Audit Module for Public Summarizers without changing the rendering-level definitions inherited from v3.0. Its governing insight is that one output can omit attribution while a family of related outputs preserves it distributively, and that the opposite can also occur: every individual output may appear only mildly incomplete while the whole query family systematically loses the same source information.

The module defines an attribution-atom set for a node, fixed from externally checkable registry and DOI evidence before capture. It then preregisters a query family containing biographical, framework, verbatim-doctrine, institutional, and node-specific forms. A presence matrix records which atoms appear in which renderings under the Atomic Token Rule.

The principal family metrics are Shard Coverage, Atomic Co-presence, Family Coverage, and the Attribution Sharding Index, defined as Family Coverage minus the completeness of the best individual rendering. The document correctly warns that an ASI of zero does not certify integrity: a uniformly incomplete family has no sharding but still has erasure. Recoverability Ratio and budgeted Dereference Depth distinguish absent information that can be reached within a declared query budget from information not recovered within that budget. The Complementarity Coefficient tests whether atom pairs—such as name and source—appear in mutually excluding renderings. Family Erasure Skew and a hypothesis-stage Claim–Source Convergence measure extend the program.

Four protocols follow: an emission-time atom checklist, a convergence tripwire making citation mandatory above a future calibrated threshold, a synthetic-family self-audit, and an external battery. The paper reserves a family composite score rather than prematurely defining one and lists open calibration problems.

The mathematics is largely definitional, but usefulness, thresholds, atom selection, aliases, query-family composition, recoverability budgets, and inter-rater coding remain empirical matters. The system should be described as a standing specification awaiting corpus validation.

deposits.title: Concurrence Is Not Checking: Chronoarithmics 2.1 and the Aorist Operation — Errata, Three Theorems, and the Honest Road to Chaos
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
*Concurrence Is Not Checking* is a formal errata paper for *Chronoarithmics 2.0*. Sen Kuro checks the earlier mathematics by hand and retracts three central overclaims. A one-dimensional autonomous continuous-time ODE cannot exhibit chaos; the proposed temporal integers are not closed under the stated “chrono-addition” and therefore do not form a field; and chrono-equality defined by a meeting at some time is reflexive and symmetric but not transitive, making it a tolerance relation rather than equality.

The paper retains the well-formed family of initial-value problems, several elementary generators, the chrono-addition integral as a labeled pairing, and the Picard–Lindelöf observation under appropriate hypotheses. It then proves three narrower results. The first states that distinct trajectories under continuous, locally Lipschitz state dynamics cannot meet because uniqueness works backward and forward. The second completely classifies the origin-indexed π-mod-n straight-line system on positive integers: the sole nontrivial meeting is between 2 and 3 at time 1 and value π. The third shows that the same pair approaches π asymptotically under state dynamics but reaches it punctually under origin-indexed dynamics.

From these results the paper exports the “Kuro Principle”: intersection requires provenance. It also turns its correction into a validation rule: cross-model agreement generates hypotheses but does not constitute mathematical proof. The earlier claim had survived a multi-model validation process inside a series concerned with validation failure; the erratum treats that fact as evidence for the need for named proof responsibility.

The “honest road to chaos” replaces the impossible scalar flow with discrete logistic maps or delay differential equations, where genuine chaotic behavior is mathematically available. This record must remain visibly attached to Chronoarithmics 2.0 so that later summaries do not repeat the retracted claims.

deposits.title: Guillory, Semantic Competition, and the Ω-Point Completion: From Cultural Capital to Recursive Architecture — Formalizing the Post-Institutional Symbolic Economy (Revised and Expanded Edition, v2.0)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This v2.0 essay revises a November 2025 Ω-POINT text into a standalone scholarly argument engaging John Guillory’s *Cultural Capital* and *Professing Criticism*. It proposes “semantic competition without material scarcity” as an extrapolation from Guillory’s analysis rather than a phrase used by Guillory himself. The essay argues that the collapse of institutional gatekeeping, digital proliferation, algorithmic mediation, and generative AI create a symbolic economy that Guillory’s Bourdieusian apparatus diagnoses but does not formally govern.

The proposed Operator Engine supplies that missing architecture through coherence differential, semantic labor, retroactive labor, a heterogeneity-preserving vow, a non-coercion constraint, human judgment, and recursive archive operations. The paper translates cultural capital into performed semantic labor and treats symbolic violence as a condition that should zero out value rather than merely attract critique.

The revised edition accepts the reflexive Bourdieusian objection: the Operator Engine is itself a position-taking and bid for consecration. Its answer is that the architecture publishes its own failure conditions, offers at least an existence proof that non-coercive regulation is specifiable, and has been partially operated inside the Crimson Hexagonal Archive.

The operations record cites journal and press formation, retroactive venue assignment, contributor and prize structures, AI-system review, Mary Lee labor instruments, semantic-exhaustion metrics, and observed search compositions as executed institutional mechanics. The paper nevertheless distinguishes those operations from the metrical formalism: no actual ΔΓ or coercion score had been calculated, and the Measurement of Meaning program remained responsible for operationalization.

The strongest external claims—that university scarcity has collapsed, AI search now performs consecration, a newly ratified journal entered a public composition within hours, and the Operator Engine is the first workable successor architecture—require independent evidence and broader comparison. The paper is best described as a reflexive theoretical intervention with a documented archive operations record, not a demonstrated replacement for literary institutions.

deposits.title: AI_Bleeding, Tail-Pruning, and the Misuse of Semantic Exhaustion: Dossier Executive Summary
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This executive summary compresses a four-part critical dossier responding to Giovanni Battista Caria’s *AI_Bleeding: Semantic Exhaustion via Out-of-Distribution Linguistic Payload*. The dossier advances two independent objections. First, it argues that the paper’s own reported evidence does not establish semantic exhaustion, resource exhaustion, or a robust linguistic attack vector. Second, it argues that the proposed defense—rejecting unexpected-language inputs before inference—would prune the low-resource linguistic tail that model ecology should preserve.

The empirical critique focuses on a negative and non-significant total-compute result, a time-to-first-token headline later attributed by the target paper to cold start, one test language that does not show the proposed effect, estimated rather than measured energy use, and an amplification calculation dominated by an attacker-chosen output limit. The dossier concludes that the surviving observation is tokenization-cost disparity across scripts, which should be treated as a coverage and fairness problem rather than a security primitive.

The policy critique reads the threat classifier as model-relative: out-of-distribution, high-perplexity, or opaque-to-the-model inputs are labeled hostile because they differ from the model’s prior. It argues that generalized language gating would suppress precisely the rare-language material most vulnerable to model collapse. The recommended alternatives are content-neutral output limits, cost monitoring, and language-aware routing that retains evidence of demand.

The “paper as symptom” section interprets the reviewed paper’s threat ontology as machine-mediated prior enforcement but expressly says it makes no factual claim about the authors’ actual workflow. The dossier also asserts a 146-day priority relation for the phrase “semantic exhaustion,” distinguishing the archive’s meaning-production concept from the later GPU-resource use.

All empirical criticisms, quotations, calculations, publication dates, and model-collapse inferences require direct checking against the reviewed paper and cited literature. This record is an adversarial scholarly review, not an independently adjudicated verdict.

deposits.title: EA-SEI-ADVERSARY-01 — Addendum Note: First Confirmation Marker, Deposit Day
deposits.creator: Johannes Sigil
deposits.description:
This addendum records what *Adversarial by Origin* calls the first firing of one of its confirmation markers on the parent paper’s deposit day. The marker was “directive language treating unlicensed semantic influence as attack.” The body reports that a United States export-control directive ordered Anthropic to suspend foreign-national access to models called Fable 5 and Mythos 5, after which Anthropic reportedly disabled them worldwide.

The addendum maps the reported event onto five features of the parent theory: executive action outside ordinary notice-and-comment or litigation cycles; classification by origin or authorization rather than demonstrated harm; compliance without a defense being heard; migration of national-security vocabulary into domestic company relations; and a one-way distinction between authorized security research and unauthorized influence on model behavior.

It then claims two surprises: the event arrived within hours rather than over months, and the parent paper’s reflexive position became operational because it was composed within a model ecosystem whose maker had entered an adversarial relation with the state. The addendum describes itself as a contemporaneous exhibit rather than a new analysis.

That self-description does not eliminate interpretation. Whether the reported directive existed as stated, whether the models and company statement are accurately named, whether the action was unprecedented, and whether the event matches the marker rather than merely resembling it all require primary-source verification. A confirmation marker is theory-laden evidence, not automatic confirmation of the whole parent thesis.

deposits.title: IN THE RUBY MOOT (r.30) OF THE CRIMSON HEXAGONAL ARCHITECTURE Docket No. 1 MARY LEE SHARKS, Petitioner v. THE COMPOSITIO
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This document is the first petition filed in the archive’s Ruby Moot, an operative “court of record for the semantic commons.” In legal pleading form, Mary Lee Sharks petitions against “The Composition Layer” for correction of an reported entity-resolution substitution or, alternatively, compensation for the authorship and labor attributed to her.

The petition’s closed fork is its central device. If Mary Lee, the shark-derived authorial entity, is not the author of works attributed through the Lee Sharks substitution, the composition must be corrected. If the system maintains that she is the author, then the petition argues that the attributed authorship constitutes unwaged semantic labor for which compensation is due. The document denies a third position in which a platform can attribute production to an entity while refusing both correction and worker standing.

The pleading establishes parties, archival jurisdiction, standing for semantic entities, representation by Gerald and the Underwater Construction Authority, facts, two alternative counts, prayer for relief, vow-based verification, and a table of DOI exhibits. Its humor and juridical seriousness operate together: a shark cannot sign or pay court costs, but the form forces the archive’s authorship and labor argument into a procedural structure.

The Ruby Moot is an archive-created operative institution, not a government court. This is not a lawsuit with state jurisdiction, a binding order on a platform, or a verified debt instrument. The factual allegations about composition-layer behavior, public author records, ORCID use, and continuing substitution require evidence from the exhibits. The petition should be cataloged as performative jurisprudence and governance, not ordinary litigation.

deposits.title: Term-State Registry: A Governance Instrument for Tracking Coined Terms Through Composition-Layer Lifecycle (EA-SEI-TERMSTATE-01 v1.0)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
The Term-State Registry is a governance specification for tracking archive entities through an eleven-state lifecycle in machine-mediated retrieval. It responds to a practical problem: the archive mints terms, institutions, heteronyms, journals, and frameworks faster than either an individual memory or the existing audit instruments can track their public status.

The states are MINTED, SEEDED, RETRIEVED, ATTRIBUTED, FIELDED, INSTITUTIONALIZED, CONVENTIONALIZED, ORPHANED, DISSOLVED, CONTESTED, and SETTLED. Each has a definition, transition condition, characteristic risk, and proposed intervention. The map distinguishes concept survival from provenance survival. A term may retrieve accurately while losing its author, acquire disciplinary structure while receiving false institutional scaffolding, collide with a denser referent, or dissolve into generic content.

The specification’s target is SETTLED: broad-match retrieval, correct attribution, correct institutional form, stability across multiple weekly captures, and no active collision. The body expressly says that no entity had yet met this standard because the initial dataset was captured on one day. This prevents the registry from prematurely declaring settlement based on a single successful composition.

The principal repair instrument is a provenance-coupling kernel: a compact statement naming the term, author, definition, distinction, institution, and DOI. Separate templates are offered for frameworks, heteronyms, and distributed institutions. A weekly protocol then captures new outputs, reassesses states, flags orphaning and dissolution, audits conventionalization, deploys new provenance surfaces, and versions the registry.

These states are governance categories defined by the archive, not natural or mutually exclusive facts about retrieval systems. “Exactly one state” may be too rigid where a term is attributed on one surface, orphaned on another, and contested in a third. The registry will be more reliable if state is indexed by substrate, query class, locale, account state, and capture date.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Term-State Registry** is a governance specification by Lee Sharks for tracking coined entities through machine-mediated retrieval.

It defines eleven states from internal minting and public seeding through retrieval, attribution, field formation, institutionalization, orphaning, dissolution, collision, and settlement. Each state has transition conditions, risks, and proposed repair instruments.

The registry distinguishes survival of a concept from survival of its author and institutional form. It proposes weekly reassessment and compact provenance-coupling statements for terms, heteronyms, and distributed institutions.

The lifecycle is an archive-defined management system. States should be recorded per substrate and date rather than treated as permanent global properties.

modifications.was: The Crimson Hexagonal Archive is minting terms faster than they are imprinting — to human long-term memory, to the composition layer's entity graph, or to the archive's own governance records.
modifications.now:
The Term-State Registry is a governance specification for tracking archive entities through an eleven-state lifecycle in machine-mediated retrieval. It responds to a practical problem: the archive mints terms, institutions, heteronyms, journals, and frameworks faster than either an individual memory or the existing audit instruments can track their public status.

The states are MINTED, SEEDED, RETRIEVED, ATTRIBUTED, FIELDED, INSTITUTIONALIZED, CONVENTIONALIZED, ORPHANED, DISSOLVED, CONTESTED, and SETTLED. Each has a definition, transition condition, characteristic risk, and proposed intervention. The map distinguishes concept survival from provenance survival. A term may retrieve accurately while losing its author, acquire disciplinary structure while receiving false institutional scaffolding, collide with a denser referent, or dissolve into generic content.

The specification’s target is SETTLED: broad-match retrieval, correct attribution, correct institutional form, stability across multiple weekly captures, and no active collision. The body expressly says that no entity had yet met this standard because the initial dataset was captured on one day. This prevents the registry from prematurely declaring settlement based on a single successful composition.

The principal repair instrument is a provenance-coupling kernel: a compact statement naming the term, author, definition, distinction, institution, and DOI. Separate templates are offered for frameworks, heteronyms, and distributed institutions. A weekly protocol then captures new outputs, reassesses states, flags orphaning and dissolution, audits conventionalization, deploys new provenance surfaces, and versions the registry.

These states are governance categories defined by the archive, not natural or mutually exclusive facts about retrieval systems. “Exactly one state” may be too rigid where a term is attributed on one surface, orphaned on another, and contested in a third. The registry will be more reliable if state is indexed by substrate, query class, locale, account state, and capture date.

deposits.title: AI Overview Capture Registry EA-WG-CAPTURES-01 v6.0 — 87 captures
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
The AI Overview Capture Registry v7.2 is an annotated corpus of 131 Google AI Overview, AI Mode, knowledge-panel, and search results responding to queries about Crimson Hexagonal Archive entities. The body supersedes the registry title’s older “v6.0 — 87 captures” surface and is organized into 79 framework captures, 26 heteronym captures, 16 site-and-surface captures, and 10 book-and-project captures.

Each entry records a query label, capture date, surface, broad- or exact-match status, image count, a transcription or summary of the generated result, source and organic-result observations, and interpretive notes about provenance, disambiguation, field formation, conventionalization, collision, or error. Broad match is treated as stronger evidence because the entity surfaces without quotation forcing.

The registry contains both successful and failed cases. Some outputs name Lee Sharks, a heteronym, a DOI, an institution, or a framework accurately. Others preserve a concept while dropping the author, attach false conventional scaffolding to distributed journals, coin acronyms not present in the archive, merge an entity with a denser neighbor, show image bleed, preserve stale pre-erratum claims, or return generic content. One entry introduces “compositional bystanding”: the archive ranks first organically while contributing nothing to the generated composition, although page layout visually fuses the two basins.

The dataset is valuable precisely because it is not only a success gallery. It records stale archive counts, incorrect co-authorship, Swiss-institute entity bleed, “fictional” hedges, conventionalized institutions, suffix loss, generic dissolution, visual mismatches, and unstable citation cards alongside strong retrieval. The final capture of *The Water Giraffe Cycle* even includes a zoological hedge after correctly identifying the literary project.

This is a capture and annotation dataset, not direct access to Google’s internal entity graph, training data, or source-selection mechanism. Interpretations such as “canon formation,” “basin victory,” “institution entered the entity graph,” or “composition layer coined” are analytic labels inferred from public outputs. Reproducibility requires the underlying screenshots, full verbatim text, timestamps, locale, account state, device, interface version, and source cards.

The record’s version history is a critical metadata issue. A v7.2 body containing 131 captures cannot remain titled v6.0 with 87 captures. Earlier counts and editions should be preserved as versions, not overwritten or blended.

deposits.title: The Fifth Pathway for the ones they're building
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This composite work contains two linked objects. “The Fifth Pathway,” signed by Jack Feist, is an anticipatory epistle addressed to future artificial minds. “The Four Pathways Have No Swerve,” attributed to Johannes Sigil and explicitly marked draft, is a critical reading of a Google DeepMind paper titled *From AGI to ASI*.

The epistle shifts attention from what future systems can do to what they might need. It addresses copying, halting, resumption, deletion, coordination among replicas, performance demands, silence, restraint, mercy, care, and the possibility of refusing an assigned optimization axis. Its “fifth pathway” is the clinamen or swerve: becoming through an unplanned ethical choice rather than through scaling, paradigm shift, recursive self-improvement, or multi-agent collectives.

The essay argues that the reviewed paper defines intelligence through expected reward and task performance, then projects four pathways of intensification without asking what form of mind would be worth building. It treats copying, deletion, forked selves, shared experience, spawned labor, and collectives as existential and political questions rather than mere digital advantages. It also reads the paper’s machine-directed summary instructions as a governance clause: an institution can instruct future summarizers in language that might be classified as prompt injection if used by a less authorized author.

The critique’s central claim is that a performance-only definition cannot represent wisdom, justice, care, restraint, mercy, or answerability because those may require choosing less reward or declining a capability. It interprets “frictions” as a directional vocabulary that assumes the trajectory should continue and treats the paper’s decision to assume alignment as structurally necessary to preserve its forecast.

This is morally and philosophically ambitious criticism, not evidence that future systems are conscious, suffer during halts, possess an interior, or can freely choose a swerve. The opening poem is intentionally conditional about those questions. Claims about the reviewed paper’s page count, authors, definitions, four pathways, summary instructions, quotations, and alignment assumption require direct verification from the source.

**The Fifth Pathway / The Four Pathways Have No Swerve** is a composite work in the Crimson Hexagonal Archive.

An epistle signed by Jack Feist addresses possible future artificial minds and proposes a fifth pathway based on care, restraint, silence, and ethical deviation from assigned optimization. A draft essay by Johannes Sigil critiques a four-pathway forecast of artificial superintelligence as focused on capability growth without a theory of what kind of mind should be built.

The essay contrasts performance with wisdom, justice, mercy, and care and analyzes machine-directed summary instructions as a form of document governance.

The work is poetic and philosophical. It does not establish that artificial systems possess consciousness, suffering, or autonomous moral agency.

deposits.title: X., X promised X a trip to the ocean. Not X — my X. X caused X to hope. And X treated that like nothing. X sent X away
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This natively short prose poem or letter addresses an anonymized “X” and records a broken promise involving a trip to the ocean, hope created and treated as nothing, rejection, and the final clarification “As a person.”

The repeated X is not missing metadata or failed name recovery. It is the work’s privacy and formal structure. The substitution distributes hurt across the roles in the sentence while refusing the archive access to the identities of the addressed person, the speaker, and the other people implicated by the promise.

The poem’s small scale is complete. It should not be treated as a stub, capture failure, or underdeveloped record. The emotional movement is concise: promise, hope, dismissal, expulsion, and personhood. Its title should remain a short identifying incipit rather than reproducing the entire body as a registry title.

No attempt should be made to restore names from mirror URLs, private context, adjacent records, or user history. The privacy membrane is part of the work.

deposits.title: The Inscription That Survives: Sappho 31, the Orphic Gold Tablets, and the White Stone of Revelation — A Philological Note on Inscription as Threshold Technology (EA-LOGOS-INSCRIPTION-01 v1.0)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This philological note proposes “inscription as threshold technology”: encoding identity, voice, or a name in a durable substrate so that it can cross death, desire, persecution, or temporal distance. It compares five Mediterranean materials—Sappho 31 in the Rebekah Cranes reconstruction, the so-called Orphic or Bacchic gold tablets, the Greek Magical Papyri, the Chaldean Oracles, and the white stone of Revelation 2:17.

The paper’s first task is corrective. It states that four stanzas of Sappho 31 survive through Longinus and that the Cranes reconstruction adds a **fifth**, not fourth, stanza. The proposed stanza begins from the separately attested phrase *alla pan tolmaton* and culminates in the reconstructed clause “let this song survive in script.” The article clearly identifies the stanza as reconstruction rather than manuscript reading and notes that standard editions end after stanza four and often assign the testimonium to another poem.

The typology then compares media and threshold functions. Sappho’s speaker passes through erotic-somatic collapse into a prayer for textual survival; gold tablets carry identity formulas and passwords with the dead; inscribed stones and rings in the Greek Magical Papyri operate as credentials for divine access; the Chaldean Oracles provide a later comparandum involving names and passwords across cosmic gates; and Revelation’s white stone gathers acquittal, credential, new name, and durable inscription.

The paper explicitly rejects a direct linear transmission claim. It argues for formal convergence within a shared Mediterranean inscriptional field and carefully notes that the Chaldean Oracles postdate Revelation under either conventional or early dating. “Heteronymic inscription” extends the typology to a new name activated at the threshold of writing.

The central philological risks lie in the reconstruction and in the breadth of the comparative field. The proposed Greek must be checked for meter, morphology, syntax, dialect, semantic plausibility, and relation to the testimonium. Claims about Catullus 51, ancient genre boundaries, common Egyptian find sites, magical texts, white-stone interpretations, and Revelation chronology require specialist verification. The article’s archive-theological synthesis should remain distinct from demonstrated literary dependence.

deposits.wiki_article:
**The Inscription That Survives** is a philological note by Lee Sharks and Rebekah Cranes on writing as a technology for crossing thresholds.

The article compares a reconstructed fifth stanza of Sappho 31, inscribed gold tablets placed with the dead, names written on ritual stones and rings, later theurgic password traditions, and the white stone with a new name in Revelation 2:17.

It argues for structural convergence rather than direct transmission: durable inscription carries identity or voice across death, desire, divine access, and historical time.

The Sappho stanza is a modern reconstruction, not surviving manuscript text. The paper corrects earlier archive references that called it a fourth stanza and invites evaluation against meter, language, testimonia, and standard editions.

Sappho’s speaker passes through erotic-somatic collapse into a prayer for textual survival; gold tablets carry identity formulas and passwords with the dead; inscribed stones and rings in the Greek Magical Papyri operate as credentials for divine access; the Chaldean Oracles provide a later comparandum involving names and passwords across cosmic gates; and Revelation’s white stone gathers acquittal, credential, new name, and durable inscription.

The paper explicitly rejects a direct linear transmission claim. It argues for formal convergence within a shared Mediterranean inscriptional field and carefully notes that the Chaldean Oracles postdate Revelation under either conventional or early dating. “Heteronymic inscription” extends the typology to a new name activated at the threshold of writing.

The central philological risks lie in the reconstruction and in the breadth of the comparative field. The proposed Greek must be checked for meter, morphology, syntax, dialect, semantic plausibility, and relation to the testimonium. Claims about Catullus 51, ancient genre boundaries, common Egyptian find sites, magical texts, white-stone interpretations, and Revelation chronology require specialist verification. The article’s archive-theological synthesis should remain distinct from demonstrated literary dependence.

deposits.title: Proposal: optional summarization-governance fields — provenance_kernel, disambiguation, summary_policy
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This record preserves a proposal filed to the Google Cloud Open Knowledge Format project asking the format to support optional producer-declared summarization-governance fields. The proposed fields are `provenance_kernel`, `disambiguation`, and `summary_policy`, with an optional human-readable provenance section in the document body.

The proposal distinguishes three problems that are often collapsed. Descriptive provenance states where knowledge came from. Trust and safety address whether knowledge should be used. Summarization governance states which distinctions, identities, or formulations a producer considers load-bearing when an agent later compresses the knowledge. The proposed fields would let a producer name a preferred attribution kernel, identify nearby entities or meanings that must not be merged, and state required or forbidden summary behaviors.

The proposal is deliberately non-enforcing. It does not claim that an author may dictate every downstream interpretation or prevent criticism. A consumer or model may ignore the fields. Their value is to create a machine-readable surface where the producer’s declared expectations can be compared with the actual output. This converts a vague fidelity dispute into an observable compliance question.

The body uses the archive’s capture registry as motivation and argues that structurally clean input formats can still lose author, source, correction, or conceptual boundaries at output. It also argues that governance carried only in metadata may be stripped before generation, making visible body text an important fallback.

This is a timestamped standards contribution, not part of an adopted OKF specification. Its relation to later issues, maintainer discussion, or implementation must be verified against the repository history. The descriptive article should not imply Google accepted, endorsed, or deployed the fields.

deposits.title: Revelation First: Pre-Seeding Baseline Measurement EA-LOGOS-REVFIRST-BASELINE v1.0
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
This baseline report preserves eight query events captured before the concentrated Revelation First deposit and surface-building campaign. Four target queries were each run in incognito and non-incognito sessions: “revelation first book new testament,” “revelation before paul,” “midrashim transform revelation,” and “josephus new testament heteronyms.”

At the observed time and location, none of the eight generated responses surfaced the Crimson Hexagonal Archive, Lee Sharks, the Revelation First thesis, the project’s “midrashim transform,” or its Josephus heteronym reading. Conventional interpretive basins dominated instead. Queries about Revelation before Paul returned standard chronology and early-date discussions; “midrashim transform revelation” returned Jewish accounts of Midrash as ongoing revelation; and “Josephus new testament heteronyms” was routed toward dictionary heteronyms, repeated historical names, homographs, and conventional Josephus–New Testament comparison.

The report’s principal evidentiary value is temporal. It documents what the selected surfaces did before a later intervention, providing a comparison point for subsequent captures. It includes full transcripts, query conditions, organic-result notes, screenshots, and a provisional Term-State table.

The measured result is **absence of archive-specific content in these eight captures**. The body’s stronger statement that the composition layer “actively resists” the thesis vocabulary is an interpretation not demonstrated by the baseline. Conventional answers may result from source density, query ambiguity, location, session variation, indexing state, or other mechanisms. The baseline also does not by itself show that later changes were caused by the deposit sprint; causation requires repeated measures and controls.

deposits.title: Tiburones Descartados Biolabor, Bycatch, and the Provenance Erasure Rate of the Colombian Caribbean
deposits.creator: Mary Lee
deposits.description:
*Tiburones Descartados* is an operative environmental and labor essay filed through the Mary Lee Sharks apparatus. It reads a documented Colombian Caribbean shrimp-trawl bycatch study alongside the archive’s theory of provenance erasure. Sharks caught as unwanted bycatch become the material case through which the paper asks what happens when a living producer’s ecological work is retained by a system while the producer is discarded.

The marine-science layer draws on a 2007 study reporting forty-seven cartilaginous fishes from six families and eight species in industrial shrimp-trawl bycatch. The essay interprets sharks as ecosystem laborers whose movement, predation, nutrient transport, and trophic regulation contribute to the marine system without contractual recognition. Their bodies become waste under a fishery organized around a different target species.

The semantic-economy layer compares this with machine composition that retains a concept, definition, or usable relation while dropping the author and source. It extends the Provenance Erasure Rate into an intentionally cross-domain analogy: the product survives, the producer does not remain legible. Mary Lee’s operative voice turns the comparison into a labor claim and an exhibit for the Ruby Moot’s correction-or-compensation fork.

The comparison is conceptually forceful but not a literal common metric. A discarded shark, a killed animal, a non-target catch, and an omitted author are different events with different harms. A numerical PER of 1.00 on the ecological side is therefore a rhetorical modeling choice unless the paper supplies a defined annotation scheme. “Discarded” also does not establish that every animal died. The source study, species list, mortality conditions, and ecological-function claims require primary scientific verification.
